blocks.text: Hello. Welcome to all visitors attending the exhibition «Ways of Reading». Before the exhibition tour begins, I’d like to ask you a question. What did you read today before attending the exhibition?

You might be thinking of a mobile phone message, the news, a sign or advertisement you saw on the street, or even a page from a book. But did you know that this natural and everyday act of ‘reading’ actually involves a meticulous design behind it? Just as we read the headlines first when we unfold the newspaper, scroll down a screen with our fingers or tap a link on our smartphones to find the next piece of content, what if someone is manipulating our view?

This question might have sounded a bit spooky, but in fact, it is design that plays the role of shaping this visual order. Design not only determines how text and images are created and arranged, but it also changes our ‘ways of reading’, what we see first and where our gaze moves next.

In this exhibition, we aim to examine how our reading habits have shaped and evolved through Korean books, magazines, newspapers, and graphic design since the 1970s. Just how closely the act of reading is linked to technology, how they have influenced each other and evolved together, shall we now explore that vast history and transformation together?
